title: Choose Incident Command AI's visual world
question: Choose the operational world that should carry the recruiter-facing war room.

options.label: Black-Box Reconstruction Table
options.lineage: aviation recorder analysis and forensic event reconstruction
options.thesis: The incident is reconstructed as a chain of evidence before anyone is allowed to act.
options.viewport: A central evidence spine joins the live severity signal, affected-service topology, causal hypotheses, and an approval rail in one continuous reconstruction surface.
options.risk: Dense forensic detail must remain instantly scannable during an active incident.

raised.raise: Numerical precision and timecode density become first-class evidence, never decoration.
Every affected service visibly traces to the dependency and countermeasure that support it.

options.label: Fireground Command Board
options.lineage: incident command tactical worksheets, unit tags, and accountability boards
options.thesis: Every responder, hazard, objective, and approval occupies a physically accountable place.
options.viewport: A broad operational board centers incident objectives, with draggable evidence tags feeding a guarded action lane and an unmistakable command clock.
options.risk: The most familiar incident metaphor can feel analog unless the evidence graph and automation are visibly alive.

options.label: Live Concourse Board
options.thesis: The whole response operation resolves into ranked live rows that visibly change when evidence changes.
options.viewport: A wall-scale status board ranks hypotheses, services, and actions by time while a selected row expands into evidence and authorization detail.
options.case: It wins immediate status recognition but holds less causal depth than the reconstruction table.
options.risk: Fixed rows can flatten the relationships that make the AI reasoning inspectable.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.thesis: The incident becomes a pure field of time, frequency, and machine evidence.
options.viewport: Evidence streams fill the frame while one selected anomaly pulls its source records into focus.
options.case: It loses operator familiarity and action clarity even though its data discipline is exceptional.
options.kept: Timecode precision and disciplined numerical hierarchy.
options.risk: The visual intensity can compete with urgent operational decisions.

options.label: Dependency Tensegrity
options.thesis: Every service failure is shown as a force traveling through dependencies and countermeasures.
options.viewport: A living dependency structure dominates the center while plans lock or release its stressed members.
options.case: It explains blast radius beautifully but loses speed for responders who need a chronological command view.
options.kept: Trace every visible failure to its dependency and countermeasure.
options.risk: Spatial novelty can obscure familiar incident chronology.

canonCard.label: Enterprise Operations Standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional dark enterprise dashboard executed with exceptional clarity.
canonCard.viewport: A navigation rail, KPI row, incident table, side detail panel, and approval drawer.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable but visually indistinguishable from many enterprise dashboards.
